title: Flicker's Fuzzy Blanket
markdown:
Willow lived in a cozy spot carved from a giant friendly mushroom in the Candlecap Mountains, where the air smelled of pine needles and warm toast. She was a young elf with dewdrop-bright eyes, sunshine hair, and pointed ears that wiggled when she got excited, which was often.

Flicker, her fluffy ginger cat, could purr loud enough to shake socks off. He chased sunbeams and never quite caught them. His most favoritest thing in the whole wide world was a fuzzy sunshine-yellow blanket embroidered with tiny bumblebees. Buzz buzz.

One cheerful morning he woke from a dream of teacup-sized butterflies, stretched paw by paw, yawned, wiggled nose to tail, and looked at the sunny window. The blanket was gone. Not even a fluff of sunshine-yellow. Big worried green eyes. Tail drooped.

“Oh no, Flicker.” Willow’s voice was wind chimes. “We will find it. A grand adventure to the Warm Lantern Woods, and home again.” She puffed her chest. Flicker offered a hopeful mrrrow, a question mark in cat.

Sunshine-yellow, bumblebee-soft. We will bring it home.

She put on her adventuring boots of soft moss that sparkled with tiny captured starlight. Flicker, with a mew that was mostly excitement, tucked himself into a little woven basket. Off they went, past whispering pines that sang secrets to the wind, and into the Warm Lantern Woods.

And oh, it was warm. Little glowing lanterns, no bigger than a thumb, hung from the branches and cast a soft golden light, tiny dancing spots on the leaves. It felt like walking inside a warm hug, or maybe a sleepy yawn. A little bird honked, a wobbly trumpet that had just woken up. Flicker blinked, curious, tail twitching. He loved new sounds.

They tiptoed along a path dotted with shiny smooth pebbles that winked in the lantern light. Whiskers twitched at every new smell: damp earth, sweet flowers, a hint of warm cookies. Suddenly a deep rumbling voice, thunder playing a gentle lullaby: “Hee hee, another loop, and this one is perfectly snuggly! Just a few more stitches, and it will be ready to wrap the whole world in cozy!”

Behind a mossy mushroom like an armchair sat an ogre, huge, mossy-green, arms like trunks, knitting on a fallen log with a long wooden needle and a rainbow of fluffy yarn: royal purple, sunny orange, sparkly blue like dragonfly wings. Click-clack, rain on a tin roof. The wool was cloud-soft.

“Hello there,” Willow said, basket steady. Flicker peeked over the edge.

Acorn-brown eyes crinkled. “Hello, little elf. And a furry friend. I’m Dermot. Knitting the longest warmest scarf in the whole wide world. Do you need a scarf? Just the right sort of breezy for a good knit.” He chuckled like pebbles downhill. Leaves fluttered from his hair.

“I’m Willow, and this is Flicker. We’re looking for his sunshine-yellow blanket, very fuzzy, with bumblebees.”

Dermot scratched, thump-thump on a mossy scalp. “Haven’t seen a blanket like that. But I baked berry buns this morning. Still warm from the twig-oven. Extra juicy.” He pulled three plump buns from a basket that smelled of sugar and summer.

Willow’s eyes widened. She gave one to Flicker, who sniffed, decided it was interesting, and nudged it happily. “Thank you. Scrumptious. Sunshine and happiness.” Flicker purred, batted a crumb out of existence.

They thanked Dermot, who waved a massive hand that felt like a soft breeze, and continued. Flicker was just starting to feel a little sad about his blanket again, tail beginning to droop, when they rounded a bend and saw another ogre, even bigger than Dermot, fast asleep. Zzzz-hummmm-zzz, like a big sleepy bee, curled near a pile of soft mossy things, a giant teddy bear taking a nap. And wait: peeking from under his enormous green arm—

Willow gasped, a little squeak. Flicker, who had been looking sleepy, perked up, ears straight. Sunshine-yellow. Fuzzy. Little embroidered bumblebees. Flicker’s blanket.

“Oh, Flicker.” A giggle escaped. “It seems another friend borrowed it for a nap. He must have thought it was the coziest thing in the whole forest.” She guessed his name might be Grumbles: all sleepy and quiet, a slightly grumpy but mostly peaceful face. He had snuggled the blanket right up close, probably dreaming of fluffy clouds and soft moss.

Sunshine-yellow, bumblebee-soft. There it is.

Willow tiptoed, moss boots silent, and with a butterfly swish pulled the blanket free. Grumbles harrumphed a puff of sleepy air and snored on. Flicker leaped from the basket, snuggled deep, and purred a song that filled the woods. He nuzzled the bumblebee with the crooked leg. Home. A grateful lick on Willow’s nose.

“Thank you for keeping it safe, Grumbles,” she whispered.

They walked back under lanterns twinkling goodnight, patterns on the path. Willow thought of cocoa with tiny marshmallows and the bestest cuddles, Flicker wrapped tight in his fuzzy sunshine-yellow bumblebee blanket, buzz buzz, all the way home.
